title: Reference and polite te
summary: Use hän and he for people and understand both uses of te.
objectives: Use hän and he without gender marking.
Recognise polite singular te with plural verb agreement.

sections.title: Hän and he are gender-neutral
paragraphs: Hän refers to one person, and he refers to more than one person. Neither pronoun marks gender.
The surrounding sentence or real-world context may identify the person, but the pronoun does not.

sections.title: Two uses of te
paragraphs: Te normally addresses more than one person. It can also address one person politely in formal situations.
Polite singular te still takes the same plural verb form as plural te. A capital Te can show special respect in some writing, but capitalization is not a separate grammar target here.
keyPoints: both uses take plural verb agreement

steps: The reference is a group of people.
Check whether a group or one politely addressed person is listening.
The same pronoun te serves both uses.

commonMistakes: Do not force an English gender distinction onto hän.
Do not use singular verb agreement with polite te.
Do not treat optional capitalization as a different pronoun.
